title: Food Dining
intro: Food ranked #2 interest. Mix of high-end and street dining within $20K budget. No dietary restrictions. September ideal for produce. Vietnam street food culture; China needs more language navigation. Hội An is a culinary destination.

bullets.heading: Hands-On Food Experiences
items: Beijing: Peking Duck ceremony at Da Dong (book 2–3 weeks ahead); hutong food walk through Nanluoguxiang
Hanoi: Old Quarter evening food walk via Ta Hien Beer Street; egg coffee ritual at Cafe Đinh or Giang
Hội An: Morning Glory Cooking School — market tour 8 AM + hands-on (~$35/person); White Rose Restaurant lunch

bullets.heading: Border Crossing Meals
items: Day 6 Beijing → Hanoi: PEK terminal 3 dining; pack snacks; pho on arrival (Pho 24 or street pho near hotel)
Day 8 Hanoi → Đà Nẵng: Metropole breakfast; eat before Noi Bai (limited airport food); resort or Mỹ Khê seafood on arrival

bullets.heading: Dining Customs — China
items: No tipping (can cause confusion); family-style shared dishes — order 1 dish per person + 1 extra
Slurping noodles shows appreciation; free tea refills — 再来一壶 (zài lái yī hú)
Meal timing: Lunch 12–1:30 PM; Dinner 6–8 PM

bullets.heading: Dining Customs — Vietnam
items: Tip 10–15% at tourist restaurants; round up at street stalls
Meals served all at once, shared; locals eat fast — don't wait for everyone
Timing: Breakfast 6–8 AM; Lunch 11:30–1 PM; Dinner 5:30–7:30 PM
Decline politely: Không, cảm ơn (No thank you)

bullets.heading: Food Safety
items: Tap water: DO NOT DRINK in either country — bottled water always
Street food: Choose busy high-turnover stalls; avoid uncovered food sitting in heat
Ice: Confirm filtered water at hotels; street stalls — ask if filtered (đá lọc)
Raw vegetables: Fine at established restaurants; caution at market stalls
